definition: Passengers divided by seats on departing flights, latest 12 months. Not the official load factor (which uses passenger-miles and seat-miles).
proxy_note: Stands in for unmet passenger demand. It is an airline outcome (pricing, fleet) and the weakest of the five inputs.

definition: Passengers in the latest 12 months compared with calendar 2019. Empty when 2019 had under 10,000 passengers.
FAA forecast boardings in fiscal 2035 compared with fiscal 2025. Used to rank airports against each other, not as a prediction: the FAA tends to over-forecast.
proxy_note: Stands in for future passenger capacity need.

definition: Arrival delays attributed to the airport and air-traffic system (BTS category NAS) divided by arriving flights, summed over the latest three years. The category is coded by airlines and includes ordinary (non-extreme) weather; it covers domestic flights of the larger reporting airlines only.
proxy_note: Stands in for flights exceeding airfield capacity. Mostly, not purely, congestion.

definition: FAA forecast commercial operations (takeoffs plus landings, cargo included) in fiscal 2035 compared with fiscal 2025. Used to rank, not as a prediction.
proxy_note: Stands in for future flight capacity need. Includes cargo flights.

definition: Position among full-data airports: half how full the planes are, a quarter passenger growth since 2019, a quarter FAA forecast passenger growth. Relative: it says where the airport stands among its peers, not that it must expand.
proxy_note: A proxy for how much added passenger capacity would be filled.

definition: Position among full-data airports: half system delay rate, half FAA forecast flight growth. Relative.
proxy_note: A proxy for how much added flight capacity would be filled.

definition: Average of the passenger-side and flight-side scores. It ranks upside (how much added capacity would be filled), a proxy for profit: no public data gives renovation cost. Size is not in the score.
proxy_note: A proxy for profit from added capacity.

definition: Passengers boarding in calendar 2025, the FAA's official count. Defines the size class.
FAA forecast boardings in fiscal 2035 minus fiscal 2025. The size of the prize in absolute terms.

display_name: Forecast extra takeoffs and landings by 2035
definition: FAA forecast commercial operations in fiscal 2035 minus fiscal 2025. FAA operations count takeoffs plus landings, so they are about double BTS departures and must not be compared with them. Includes cargo.
Arriving flights 15 or more minutes late, from any cause, divided by arriving flights, latest three years.

display_name: System delay rate - latest 12 months only
definition: The system delay rate over the latest 12 months only. One year swings a lot, so the three-year value drives the score.
Departing flights that are not passenger flights divided by all departing flights. Cargo shares the runways but is not in the score.

Departing passenger flights of 3,000 miles or more divided by all departing passenger flights, domestic plus international. There is no official definition of long-haul; the cutoff is ours and adjustable.
The biggest airline's passengers divided by all passengers. Dependence on one airline is a risk.
Passengers to US destinations divided by all departing passengers, latest 12 months.
Passengers on board departing flights, latest 12 months. Through passengers are counted on each leg, so this can exceed FAA boardings.
Seats on departing flights in the latest 12 months compared with calendar 2019.
Departing passenger flights in calendar 2025 compared with calendar 2019.
Passengers divided by departing passenger flights, calendar 2025. Rising with flat flights means bigger planes.
